% Typed shift stepsize (TSS): a statistical procedure, not a dashboard.
% Estimators, signed LR map, and the scheduler comparison.
% Requires amsmath, booktabs. Table~\ref{tab:tss-vs-schedulers} is auto-generated.

\paragraph{Typed shift stepsize.}
Let $W$ index consecutive batches and let $X=(X^{(v)},X^{(a)},X^{(t)})$ be the concatenated video/audio/text block.
Covariate shift on modality $m$ is a change in $P(X^{(m)}\mid W)$.
Concept drift on modality $m$ is a change in $P(Y\mid X^{(m)})$.
These are different identified objects and they must not share a learning-rate sign.

\emph{Covariate intensity.}
Let $z_i^{(m)}$ be the coordinate-mean of block $m$ on window $i$.
The two-sample Cohen statistic
\begin{equation}
  \hat c_m
  =
  \bigl|\,d\bigl(z^{(m)}\mid W=t-1,\; z^{(m)}\mid W=t\bigr)\bigr|
\end{equation}
is an absolute intensity, not a simplex share.
The share $\pi_m=\hat c_m/\sum_{m'}\hat c_{m'}$ remains a \emph{which-head} budget (open vision, then audio, not clip-level text).
Using $\eta_m=\eta_0\pi_m$ has the wrong sign whenever the map $P(Y\mid X^{(m)})$ is still valid.

\emph{Concept intensity.}
Translate the new block to the old mean, $\tilde X_t^{(m)}=X_t^{(m)}-(\bar x_t^{(m)}-\bar x_{t-1}^{(m)})$.
A pure location shift in $P(X^{(m)})$ is removed by that alignment; a change in $P(Y\mid X^{(m)})$ is not.
Fit a unimodal ridge head on ANOVA-screened coordinates of one half of batch $t-1$ and evaluate 0-1 risk on the other half ($R_{t-1}$) and on $\tilde X_t^{(m)}$ ($R_t^{\mathrm{al}}$):
\begin{equation}
  \hat\delta_m
  =
  \bigl(R_t^{\mathrm{al}}-R_{t-1}\bigr)_+.
\end{equation}
In-sample CE of a joint SGD probe is not a concept estimator: it confuses generalization gap with a change in $P(Y\mid X)$.

\emph{Signed stepsize.}
With a quiet hold when both channels are off,
\begin{equation}
  \eta_m^{(t+1)}
  =
  \begin{cases}
    \eta_m^{(t)}
      & \text{if }\hat c_m<\tau_c\text{ and }\hat\delta_m<\tau_\delta,\\[0.35em]
    \eta_0\dfrac{1+\beta\hat\delta_m}{1+\lambda\hat c_m}
      & \text{otherwise.}
  \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Quiet means \emph{do not retune} the step, not $\eta_m=0$.
The weights keep moving at last epoch's rate; the schedule itself is frozen until a channel speaks.
Large $\hat c_m$ lowers the step (do not chase $X$).
Large $\hat\delta_m$ raises the step (relearn the map).
Clip-level text on the MSR-VTT extract is both-quiet, so $\eta_t$ stays at the warmup scale rather than being inverted from $\pi_t\approx 0$.

Refresh / KV invalidation is a different control: it may still follow $\hat c_m$.
TSS is the SGD map, not a memory schedule, and not a cosine lag board.

\emph{Comparators.}
Constant, step decay, cosine annealing, inverse-time, and a plateau rule (halve $\eta$ after two non-improving rounds) are scalar schedulers of $t$ or of the loss.
They cannot type the shift.
$\eta\propto\pi$ uses the same $\hat c_m$ with the opposite sign.
Oracle TSS substitutes the known $(c_m,\delta_m)$ of the simulation DGP.
Table~\ref{tab:tss-vs-schedulers} reports the Monte Carlo comparison.
On covariate-only streams the target is backward transfer (accuracy on batch~0 after the stream); on concept-only streams it is post-change accuracy.

\emph{Next epoch only.}
The map is applied to epoch $t+1$.
Batch $t$ is used to estimate $(\hat c,\hat\delta)$ with the frozen probe; the step taken on batch $t$ still uses $\eta^{(t)}$ from the previous pair.
Global clocks (cosine, plateau) are functions of $t$ and copy one scalar onto every head.

\emph{Per-head scheduler logic.}
The same classical clocks can be kept \emph{per modality}: plateau$_m$ halves $\eta_m$ after two non-improving unimodal CE rounds; restart$_m$ is cosine with a per-head SGDR reset when $\hat\delta_m$ jumps; Polyak$_m$ sets $\eta_m$ proportional to unimodal CE.
inv-$c$ is the covariate half of TSS ($\beta=0$).
None of these type both channels at once, which is the only thing TSS adds.

\emph{Other opportunities, not claimed here.}
EWC / SI (raise a quadratic penalty when $\hat c_m$ is large, instead of shrinking $\eta_m$); Fisher-scaled or natural-gradient steps on the same split; Hedge / EXP3 over heads; a two-timescale freeze of high-$\hat c$ towers.
Those are the next knobs on the same $(c_m,\delta_m)$ pair, not a different product loop.
A second labelled extract is required before claiming a downstream-task magnitude; the present MSR-VTT windows illustrate $\hat c$ and the quiet text \emph{hold}, not a finished applied study.
